Access.description: Whether a rule grants or revokes access.

AllowedValue.description:
A single allowed value with an optional per-option description and extra
presentation fields selected by `TOpt`.

Serializes as a struct; deserializes from either the full struct form or a
bare value shorthand (RFC 0003 §5.4):

```yaml
# bare shorthand:
allowed: [mit, apache-2.0]

# full struct (generator):
allowed:
  - value: mit
    name: MIT
  - value: apache-2.0
    description: "Permissive, patent grant"
```

ArrayBody.description:
Body shared by all array variants: optional allowed-value list and default.

`T` is the element type (`String`, `i64`, `f64`).
`TOpt` is the per-option extra type from the active `InputProfile`.

No `Eq` or `Hash` derives — `T` may be `f64`.

allowed.description: When `Some` the input is constrained to this list; `None` → free entry.

BaseInput.description:
The presentation-free fields shared by every `Input<E>` variant.

`message` is deliberately absent — it is presentation and lives in `E::Base`.

Deserialization is implemented manually (not derived) so that
`serde_path_to_error` can track field paths through the
`#[serde(flatten)]` boundary used by all `*Input<E>` variant structs.
The flatten machinery passes a `FlatMapDeserializer` here; wrapping it
with `serde_path_to_error` before dispatching to the inner struct
ensures errors in e.g. `validators[0].condition` carry the full path.

description.description: Machine-facing help text; emitted as `description` in JSON Schema.

name.description: Unique key used in the resolved-value map.  Must match `[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*`.

secret.description:
When `true` the value must not be logged, echoed, cached, or persisted.
Maps to `writeOnly: true` in the JSON Schema projection.

validators.description: Zero or more Tera validator expressions run against the resolved value.

CapabilitiesStrictness.description:
How strictly to treat a **capability floor gap** — a governed domain that,
on the resolved runtime/platform, ends up enforced only by a *bypassable*
in-process mechanism (the RPC broker or the script shim) with no
un-bypassable runtime-flag or OS-sandbox floor. Examples: `net`/`process` on
Bun (no permission model), or any governed domain off-Linux while no
OS-sandbox backend covers it.

The variants are ordered `Warn < RequireFloor`, so `strictness` can be
combined across configuration levels by taking the [`max`](Ord::max) — the
most-severe stance any enclosing level declared wins.

oneOf.description:
Proceed, surfacing each floor gap as a non-fatal warning. Enforcement is
still active as defense in depth. This is the shipped default.

Refuse to run when any governed domain lacks an un-bypassable floor for
the resolved runtime/platform: a run proceeds only when every governed
domain is floored (so the confinement cannot be bypassed by raw sockets,
direct syscalls, or FFI/N-API/WASM).

CapabilityDomain.description:
An abstract capability domain — the universal vocabulary shared by every
subsystem and every enforcement backend.

oneOf.description: Creating / writing / removing files and directories.

CapabilityPolicyConfig_tool.description: A level's capability policy: an ordered list of allow/deny rules plus a floor-gap strictness stance.

CapabilityRules_tool.description: An ordered list of allow/deny capability rules. Levels cascade by concatenation; a matching deny always wins.

allOf.description:
The subsystem-neutral body of a single capability entry.

`patterns` are platform-neutral: filesystem globs (`@workspace/**`),
`host:port` for [`Net`](CapabilityDomain::Net), or plain names/globs for
[`Env`](CapabilityDomain::Env) / [`Process`](CapabilityDomain::Process).

access.description: Whether this rule grants (`allow`) or revokes (`deny`) access.

direct.description:
Lower this specific pattern to a scoped OS grant so the runtime can read
or `import()` it directly, without brokering every access. Defaults to
`false`, in which case the pattern stays broker-mediated (and, on
platforms without a kernel filesystem floor, is surfaced as a floor gap
rather than lowered). Only meaningful for filesystem-read rules.

domain.description: The capability domain this rule governs.

on_unenforceable.description:
What to do if this rule cannot be faithfully enforced on the current
platform. `None` inherits the caller's default (the fail-closed `deny`).

patterns.description:
Neutral patterns matched against the request (fs globs, `host:port`, or
names). An empty list matches nothing.

NoExtra.description:
A flattenable empty extras type.

We deliberately do *not* use `()` for the flattened extra slots: serde's
`#[serde(flatten)]` on a unit type fails to deserialize from a map, whereas
an empty braced struct flattens cleanly (and ignores unknown keys).

anyOf.description: A structural reference into pipeline inputs or an earlier step's output.
A literal or Tera-templated string rendered to a string.

PipelineInputValue.description:
A value supplied to a pipeline step's input.

Two kinds are disambiguated structurally:

* a structural reference (`{ from: "steps.<name>.output.<path>" }` or
  `{ from: "inputs.<name>" }`) that preserves the referenced JSON value's
  type; and
* a literal scalar or a Tera-string that is rendered to a string.

PipelineOutput.description: How a `type: pipeline` tool surfaces its result.

oneOf.description: Return the last non-skipped step's output (the default).
Return an object mapping every step name to its output.

PipelineStep.description: A single step in a `type: pipeline` tool.

if.description:
Optional Tera boolean condition. A falsy result skips the step and makes
its output resolve to `null` for later references.

inputs.description: Inputs handed to the invoked tool, by input name.

name.description: Unique name; referenced by later steps via `from: steps.<name>.output`.

tool.description: The name of the tool this step invokes.

ToolJsRuntime.description:
Which JavaScript runtime to launch a tool's entrypoint with.

**Only [`Deno`](Self::Deno) is currently fully supported**, and it is the
default for tools. Deno is the sole runtime whose sandboxing — filesystem,
network, environment, and child-process confinement — is complete on Linux,
macOS, and Windows today.

`node` and `bun` are accepted for compatibility but are **experimental and
discouraged**: their confinement is incomplete or absent, so selecting one
(or resolving to one via [`Auto`](Self::Auto)) emits a warning. They are
omitted from the JSON schema so editors do not suggest them, but the values
remain valid if set explicitly.

oneOf.description:
The Deno runtime — the recommended, fully-confined runtime on all
platforms. The default for tools.

UnenforceablePolicy.description:
What to do when a rule's pattern turns out to be **genuinely unenforceable**
— i.e. no selected enforcement backend (pre-spawn flags, OS sandbox, or
in-process broker) can faithfully confine it on the current platform.

This is a *policy* decision owned by the author of the rule, not by any
particular enforcement mechanism, which is why it lives in the core model
even though the core itself never acts on it: the enforcement layer reads it
when composing a plan (see `omni_capability_enforcement`).

Variants are ordered by severity (`Allow` < `Warn` < `Deny`) so that when the
same pattern is governed by several rules, the most severe choice wins.

oneOf.description: Proceed silently, dropping the unenforceable pattern (least confinement).
Proceed, but surface a warning for the pattern that will not be enforced.

Refuse to run and report the unenforceable pattern. **Default** — if we
cannot confine it, we do not run it.

ValidateConfiguration.description:
A single validator expression applied to an input value.

`condition` is evaluated as a boolean — `true` means the value is valid.
`error_message` is rendered as a Tera template when the condition is false;
if absent a default message is generated.

condition.description:
Tera expression evaluated to a boolean; `true` = value is valid.

Available context: `value` — the candidate value.

error_message.description:
Tera expression rendered as the error message when `condition` is false.

Available context: `value` — the candidate value.

description:
A discovered tool manifest (`tool.omni.yaml`).

The `name`, `description`, `inputs`, and `capabilities` fields are shared by
every backend; the backend-specific fields are flattened in from
[`ToolBackend`] behind the required `type` discriminant.

oneOf.description:
A JavaScript entrypoint whose default export is invoked and whose return
value is captured.

entrypoint.description: Path to the runnable JavaScript entrypoint, relative to the manifest.

runtime.description: The JavaScript runtime to launch. Defaults to `deno`.

oneOf.description: A sequence of steps that chain other tools together.

output.description: How the pipeline surfaces its result. Defaults to `last`.

steps.description: Ordered steps executed in declaration order.

capabilities.description:
Capability policy governing what this tool may do (filesystem / process
/ network / environment access). Cascades under the workspace-level
tool policy; a matching `deny` always wins.

description.description: Human-readable description of what the tool does.

inputs.description: Typed, validated, non-interactive inputs (the data-only input model).
